findings.who: A filer held a coin through an exchange when it hard-forked in 2024. The exchange did not support the new coin until 2025, when it credited the forked units to the filer's account.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether 'In 2025' they got 'new coins from a fork'. The filer dates the fork to 2024, so they answer no. Under the IRS ruling, though, the coins were received in 2025, when the filer first gained dominion and control.
findings.irs_text: rr-2019-24 p. 3: "If the taxpayer later acquires the ability to transfer, sell, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the cryptocurrency, the taxpayer is treated as receiving the cryptocurrency at that time."
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Count forked or airdropped coins in the year they first showed up in a wallet or account you could use, even if the fork or airdrop happened earlier.'

findings.who: A filer received tokens in a promotional airdrop or project 'giveaway' that the issuer marketed as free or as a gift. Or the filer received crypto tips or donations from strangers for online content they made as a hobby, not a business.
findings.why_no: The help's No list says 'getting it as a gift'. A giveaway or tip feels like a gift, and the gate's help does not limit the gift exception to a gift from a person, as the gated question's help does.
findings.irs_text: rr-2019-24 p. 5, Holding (2): "A taxpayer has gross income, ordinary in character, under § 61 as a result of an airdrop"; i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v: "If, in 2025, you received ordinary income in connection with digital assets that isn't reported elsewhere on your return ... report this income on line 8v."
findings.fix: Narrow the help's No item to 'getting it as a personal gift from a family member or friend, or as an inheritance'. Add: 'Airdrops, giveaways, promotions and tips are not gifts. Answer Yes.'

findings.who: A filer holds a liquid-staking or rebasing token, or leaves coins in an exchange 'earn' or auto-staking program. Their balance grows on its own and they never took any action.
findings.why_no: The filer sees themselves as only holding, and the help's No list includes 'holding'. They do not perceive automatic balance growth as getting 'a reward or new coins'.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 16: "Received new digital assets as a result of mining, staking, and similar activities"; i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v: "income from forks, staking, or mining"
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Yes also if your crypto balance grew on its own in 2025, such as from automatic staking, an exchange earn or rewards program, or a rebasing or liquid-staking token. Holding counts as No only if the number of coins did not grow.'

findings.who: A filer lent crypto on a lending platform or a decentralized-finance protocol, or provided liquidity there, and received yield or interest paid in crypto in 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate names 'pay, a reward or new coins', and the help's Yes list mentions only pay, staking, mining, forks and airdrops. The filer reads interest or yield as none of these and answers no. The IRS question covers receipt 'as ... payment for property', which reaches yield for lending property.
findings.irs_text: f1040 p. 1, Digital Assets: "did you: (a) receive (as a reward, award, or payment for property or services)"; i1040gi p. 92, Line 8v: "ordinary income in connection with digital assets that isn't reported elsewhere on your return"
findings.fix: Add 'interest, yield or lending or liquidity rewards, prizes, referral or learn-and-earn bonuses' to the Yes help. Also broaden the gated question beyond staking, mining, forks and airdrops.

locators: Form 1040 (2025), page 1, Digital Assets, "At any time during 2025, did you: (a) receive (as a reward, award, or payment for property or services); or (b) sell, exchange, or otherwise dispose of a digital asset (or a financial interest in a digital asset)?"; , Digital Assets, "Digital assets are any digital representations of value that are recorded on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger or any similar technology."; , "Received new digital assets as a result of mining, staking, and similar activities", "Disposed of a digital asset in exchange or trade for another digital asset", "Holding a digital asset in a wallet or account" and "Purchasing digital assets using U.S. or other real currency"

p. 15, Digital Assets, "Check the “Yes” box next to the question on digital assets on page 1 of Form 1040 or 1040-SR if at any time during 2025, you (a) received (as a reward, award, or payment for property or services)"; p. 16, "Received new digital assets as a result of mining, staking, and similar activities; • Received digital assets as a result of a hard fork"

p. 92, Line 8v, "If, in 2025, you received ordinary income in connection with digital assets that isn’t reported elsewhere on your return (for example, digital assets, such as income from forks, staking, or mining, which aren’t wages reported on line 1a or capital gain or loss reported on Form 8949 and Schedule D), report this income on line 8v."; , Holding (2), "A taxpayer has gross income, ordinary in character, under § 61 as a result of an airdrop of a new cryptocurrency following a hard fork if the taxpayer receives units of new cryptocurrency"

findings.who: A filer who made joint estimated tax payments with a spouse or former spouse and is now filing separately or single, especially if the spouse or former spouse sent the payments.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'by you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)' and the filer reads spouse/former-spouse payments as counting only on a joint return, so they answer no because they are not filing jointly.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 26: 'If you and your spouse paid joint estimated tax but are now filing separate income tax returns, you can divide the amount paid in any way you choose as long as you both agree.'
findings.fix: Drop the 'on a joint return' limitation and say: include estimated tax paid jointly with a spouse or former spouse even if you are now filing separately; enter your agreed share.

findings.who: A surviving spouse filing a joint return for 2025 whose deceased spouse made 2025 estimated tax payments or had a 2024 overpayment applied.
findings.why_no: The gate refers to 'your spouse' only in the present tense and the help does not mention a deceased spouse; the filer may answer no because the spouse has died.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 26: 'Follow these instructions even if your spouse died in 2025 or in 2026 before filing a 2025 return.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate/help: include payments made by a spouse who died in 2025 or 2026 if you file a joint return.

findings.who: A filer who made a 2025 estimated tax payment in January 2025, an early Q1 payment, rather than in January 2026.
findings.why_no: The help says 'including one in January 2026 but not a January 2025 payment for 2024'; the filer may read the January 2025 exclusion as covering any January 2025 payment.
findings.irs_text: f1040 (2025) p. 2, line 26: '2025 estimated tax payments and amount applied from 2024 return'; i1040gi p. 39: 'Enter any estimated federal income tax payments you made for 2025.'
findings.fix: Say: a January 2025 payment counts if it was designated for 2025; only a January 2025 payment for 2024 does not.

findings.who: A filer who made a late 2025 estimated tax payment in February 2026 or later, before filing the 2025 return.
findings.why_no: The help gives only 'including one in January 2026' as the post-year example; the filer may read that as the only post-2025 payment date that counts.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 26: 'Enter any estimated federal income tax payments you made for 2025.'
findings.fix: Say: include any estimated tax payment for 2025 made after 2025, not only one in January 2026.

locators: Form 1040 (2025), line 26; , Line 26, "If you or your spouse paid separate estimated tax but you are now filing a joint return, add the amounts you each paid"

used.how: pages named by another document's citation

findings.who: Filer has only exempt-interest dividends from a municipal bond mutual fund, reported in Form 1099-DIV box 12, and no Form 1099-INT box 8 or Form 1099-OID amount.
findings.why_no: The gate help says those fund dividends are 'asked with dividends,' so the filer answers no to tax-exempt interest; if the dividends gate asks ordinary dividends, box 12 is not ordinary either, so the amount can fall through both.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi (2025) p. 25, line 2a: 'Also include on line 2a any exempt-interest dividends from a mutual fund or other regulated investment company. This amount should be shown in box 12 of Form 1099-DIV.'
findings.fix: Broaden this gate/help to include exempt-interest dividends (Form 1099-DIV box 12), or make the dividends question explicitly collect box 12 and add it to line 2a.

findings.who: Filer holds a tax-exempt zero-coupon bond and receives a Form 1099-OID showing tax-exempt OID in box 2 or box 11, but no cash interest payment was made in 2025.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether they 'get' tax-exempt interest; the filer reads that as cash received and answers no because OID is not paid in cash.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi (2025) p. 25, line 2a: 'including any tax-exempt original issue discount (OID)... your tax-exempt OID should be shown in box 11 of Form 1099-OID. Enter the total on line 2a.'
findings.fix: Ask about tax-exempt interest or OID reported to the filer, and state that OID counts even if no cash is received.

findings.who: Filer receives tax-exempt interest through a trust or partnership Schedule K-1, or from a direct municipal loan or below-threshold payment, so no Form 1099-INT box 8 or Form 1099-OID was issued.
findings.why_no: The help names only Box 8 of Form 1099-INT and Form 1099-OID boxes 2 and 11, so the filer answers no when no such form was received.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi (2025) p. 25, line 2a: 'If you received any tax-exempt interest... Enter the total on line 2a.'
findings.fix: Ask the fact rather than the form; add that tax-exempt interest reported on a Schedule K-1 or received without a 1099-INT/OID still belongs on line 2a.

locators: Instructions for Form 1040, p. 25, line 2a, "Enter the total on line 2a" (Form 1099-INT box 8, Form 1099-OID boxes 2 and 11, net of amortized bond premium and acquisition premium)

findings.who: A filer whose W-2 shows Additional Medicare Tax withheld (Form 8959, line 24) and no non-wage withholding.
findings.why_no: The gate asks for federal income tax taken out of money other than wages; Additional Medicare Tax is Medicare tax and is withheld from wages, so the truthful answer is no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 25c—Other Forms: 'Additional Medicare Tax you had withheld. Include the amount shown on Form 8959, line 24, in the total on line 25c.'
findings.fix: Do not gate the Additional Medicare Tax component on this question; remove the line-25c help saying to leave it out, and add a separate ungated input for Form 8959 line 24 that flows to line 25c.

findings.who: A filer with a 2025 Form 1099-OID, or a 1099-B for barter, showing federal income tax withheld in box 4 on accrued or non-cash income but no money paid to them.
findings.why_no: They read 'money paid to you' literally, see that no cash was paid, and answer no; the help only says 'Box 4 of a Form 1099' without saying non-cash or accrued 1099 income also counts.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 25b: 'If you received a 2025 Form 1099 showing federal income tax withheld on ... other income you received, include the amount withheld in the total on line 25b.'
findings.fix: Ask whether any Form 1099 box 4 shows federal income tax withheld, regardless of whether cash was paid, and state that non-cash or accrued 1099 income counts.

findings.who: A filer with federal income tax withheld on an IRA distribution (Form 1099-R) or on dividends or interest (Form 1099-DIV or 1099-INT), not a pension, social security, unemployment, or gambling winning.
findings.why_no: They read the gate’s list—'such as a pension, social security, unemployment or gambling winnings'—as the complete set and answer no because their 1099 is not one of those examples.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 25b: 'If you received a 2025 Form 1099 showing federal income tax withheld on dividends, taxable or tax-exempt interest income ... include the amount withheld in the total on line 25b.'
findings.fix: Replace the short example list with a broad form-based prompt: any Form 1099 series (1099-R, 1099-DIV, 1099-INT, 1099-G, 1099-B, 1099-K, 1099-MISC, etc.) showing box 4 withholding.

findings.who: An executor or guardian filing a final or fiduciary Form 1040 for a decedent or incapacitated person who had a 2025 Form 1099-R or SSA-1099 with federal income tax withheld.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether tax was taken out of money paid to 'you'; the money was paid to the decedent or ward, not to the person answering, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 39, Line 25b: 'Include on line 25b any federal income tax withheld on your Form(s) 1099-R.'
findings.fix: Ask about the taxpayer, including a decedent or incapacitated person for whom the return is filed, and keep the joint-return spouse language.
